title: Living witness
passages:
The service rig's drive tires bit the drainage shoulder's loose gravel, fishtailing once before Ospina caught it. They'd run 7-K hard from Kettering — two hundred klicks of washboard haul road with the chipped die warm in their coat pocket and Kass's badge 2241 burning a hole in the named-rider slot. The unmarked cradle rig sat square across the lane ahead, Pell's silhouette black against the work lights spilling from Anza's ore siding.

Ospina didn't brake. They clipped the cradle rig's rear corner at thirty klicks, a sound like a shipping container dropped from a crane. Metal screamed. 7-K's bumper folded. The cradle rig slewed sideways, its stabilizers digging furrows in the hardpan.

"Channel holding," Kass said. Their voice came tight through the named-rider link, backgrounded by the dish array's proximity alarm — a rising whine that meant the comms mast was three seconds from auto-fold. "Near-end warning. Two minutes to line-of-sight loss."

Ospina killed 7-K's momentum with a jab of the retarder, swung the nose into the siding's unlit throat. The ore stub's switch lights showed red over red. Dead track. Good. They'd have to come on foot.

"Pell's moving," Kass said. "He's turning his rig. Coming in behind us."

The dish screamed its final warning and folded. The named-rider channel dropped to carrier-wave only — no voice, no data, just a heartbeat ping that meant *alive, waiting*. Kass's fingers never left the console.

Ospina killed 7-K's engine. Silence rushed in, thick with dust and the smell of hot hydraulic fluid. They palmed the door release, stepped down into the siding's shadow. The chipped die pressed against their ribs through the coat lining. One corner chipped, the pattern shifted. The forger's own tool. The only thing that could unmake what the forger had made.

Ahead, the relay shop's floodlights cut a rectangle across the yard. Teodoro stood in the doorway, dispatch line in one hand, pod plate in the other. At the med rig's flank, Rhea's hand rested on seal K-7745, winch cable slack. Marlowe sat on the rig's lower step, shoulder braced, watching the siding mouth.

Pell's cradle rig crunched into the siding behind them, tires grinding ballast. Its door threw open.

Ospina didn't turn. They walked toward the shop, boots loud on the ties. Let him follow. The die in their pocket was the only warrant that mattered now.
